title: WorldWideWeb browser and the first website (CERN)
lede: Tim Berners-Lee’s first browser and the CERN project page it displayed: the unstyled hypertext that web brutalism looks back to.
summary: CERN, 1990–1991: black text on white, underlined links, a plain heading, and a two-column link list.
made: 1990–1991 (browser and first pages); 2019 (CERN rebuild in a modern browser)

evidence.note: Opened Wikimedia Commons “[W3 First Website.png](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:W3_First_Website.png)” (1366 × 655 px, uploaded 8 November 2021) with the Read tool on 2026-10-02. It shows the first project page, info.cern.ch/hypertext/WWW/TheProject.html, in CERN’s 2019 browser rebuild, not on original NeXT hardware. Also viewed “WorldWideWeb.1.png” (834 × 642 px), a screenshot of the original NeXTSTEP application’s panels.

styles.note: Lineage: the unintended original of the look. Smashing Magazine (2020) calls the first website an “inadvertent disciple”.

notice: This is a lineage reference. The page was plain because early HTML had no styling, not by choice. Its sans-serif rendering comes from NeXTSTEP, not from later browser defaults.
context: [Smashing Magazine (2020)](ref:smashing-split-personality-brutalist-web-2020) names the first website as the first example of raw-HTML brutalism.

Commons tags both screenshots as public domain because “the whole project was released into the public domain in 1993”, citing CERN document record 1164399. That record was behind a bot check on 2026-10-02 and was not read. The NeXTSTEP screenshot itself shows “Copyright 1990,91,93,94, TBL, CERN. Distribution restricted: ask for terms.”
observed: In the rebuild, a white document window with a black title bar sits on a dark gray desktop beside a gray menu column (Info, Navigate, Document, Edit, Links, Style, Print).
The page has a bold, centered sans-serif heading, “World Wide Web”, and two indented paragraphs of black text.
Below them, a two-column list pairs underlined link titles (What’s out there?, Help, Software Products, Technical, Bibliography) with plain descriptions.
Links are black and underlined. There is no color, image, rule, or box on the page.
interpretation: The first page already shows the core of [Brutalist web design](style:brutalist-web-design): structure carried only by headings, paragraphs, lists, and underlines. Blue links came later, with browsers such as [NCSA Mosaic](ref:ncsa-mosaic-browser-1993).
borrow: Write link text that says where the link goes, and put a one-line plain description next to it.

rights.statement: Commons tags the screenshots public domain, but the status of the depicted interface is unclear (see context). Viewed at the source; not stored.
